title: Project-aware six gates and current-head check evidence
acceptance: Implement design section 15: --project selects clone, base and pinned scope/contract. Gates 1 and 2 use project or stacked PR base; gate 4 verifies pins; gate 5 uses pinned complete contract including docs and fail-first. Gate 3 stays retired with usage error. Gate 6 combines required check-runs and commit statuses on verified current SHA, resolving required names from readable protection and confirmed conventions. Missing/pending is pending, failed is failed, unreadable is unknown. Gate 7 consumes authenticated local final verdict evidence (T-135 records with T-138 external signing/patch binding), honoring project review policy; comments alone are not authority.

Move self T-043 top-level project block unchanged to projects.firstmate-workflow.project and delete top-level block in the same commit. Exactly one self contract source remains; old pins read the location at their recorded commit without repinning. Resolve external contracts from approved private project snapshots, never publish them in the engine registry. Update README accordingly.

Update section 6 and README: gate 5 reads pinned contract, never tested branch or mutable engine copy. Scope may permit config changes without letting a branch alter its own gates. Preserve old self pins across top-level to registry transition.

Preserve self-project commands and gate budgets; no gate 3 execution or budget returns. Pin/contract hash failures name their reason. Before current-head acceptance, synchronize and verify the authoritative GitHub PR head against the local task ref and isolated checkout. Bind required check-runs AND commit statuses, gates, reviewed head/base/patch, reviewer identity/final-answer provenance and merge candidate to that verified SHA. If remote moves or cannot be verified, readiness is stale/unknown; refresh before accepting. Regression: GitHub update-branch moves remote while local ref remains stale; green local gates must not pass remote readiness. Approval carries only when authoritative current patch-id is unchanged and no later rejection supersedes it. Merge candidate binding is enforced at merge time by T-138 (`bin/fm-merge.sh`).
Self-hosting keeps working after this task alone: with no --project, and with the firstmate-workflow project named explicitly, every existing caller, fixture and test behaves as before.
Evidence is this pull request's required GitHub check and the six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7. New behaviour gets tests written to fail first; the worker does not run the suite itself.
Stay inside this scope. If the work needs a file outside it, stop and name the file and the reason.

External project data lives only under FM_HOME/projects/<name>/{repo,worktrees,CONVENTIONS.md,tasks,design.md,state}. No private specs, worktrees, prompts, pins, evidence, mirrors or recovery data in engine state or its public tree. Private repos are accepted. Unreadable protection is unknown: require captain-confirmed project checks and policy before readiness, never infer permission or reject solely for visibility. Every GitHub operation names the project repository. Preserve self-project default and explicit-name compatibility. Never push to protected base; task-branch force-with-lease requires confirmed project policy and expected old head. Merge method, deletion, land/review/post and stacking follow CONVENTIONS.md, never hardcoded squash/delete.

Evidence: required GitHub checks and commit statuses plus six gates 1,2,4,5,6,7 on the authoritative current PR head; gate 3 is retired. Workers author feature-owned fail-first tests but run no suites. Tests stay at most 1200 lines; shared fixtures in tests/lib/ or tests/e2e/lib/, with literal helper references. Firstmate verifies CI/gates and real acceptance; a structure check cannot prove model compliance. Commit this task spec with implementation.
